text: The number of goals scored by a team in a match is independent of other matches, and is denoted by
the random variable X, which has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.36. A supporter offers to make
a donation of $5 to the team for each goal that they score in the next 10 matches.
Find the expectation and standard deviation of the amount that the supporter will pay. [5]

Assuming that the standard deviation of journey times is still 0.12 hours, test at the 2.5%

text: In the past, the time, in hours, for a particular train journey has had mean 1.40 and standard deviation
0.12. Following the introduction of some new signals, it is required to test whether the mean journey
time has decreased.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Assume that the number of accidents per year follows a Poisson distribution.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State null and alternative hypotheses for a test of Jane’s claim.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Test at the 5% significance level whether Jane’s claim is justified.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Jane finds that the number of accidents per year has been gradually increasing over recent years.
State how this might affect the validity of the test carried out in part (a)(ii).

text: The local council claims that the average number of accidents per year on a particular road is 0.8.
Jane claims that the true average is greater than 0.8. She looks at the records for a random sample of
3 recent years and finds that the total number of accidents during those 3 years was 5.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate a 98% confidence interval for the population mean.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why it was necessary to use the Central Limit theorem in answering part (b).

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Find the probability that the confidence interval found in part (b) is wholly above the true value
of the population mean.
